newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on local buying.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on local buying.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Thursday on local buying but Western investors held back, traders said.

The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 2.19 percent to 286.47 on $46.71 million in volume. Utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS edged up to $1.46 at Thursday's close from $1.44 at Wednesay's close.
Russian banks remained major buyers on the market restraining it from correction, traders said. Domestic brokers have begun buying, dismissing the probability of further correction, traders said.
"Russian operator activity is very high," said Regent European Securities chief trader Dmitry Starenko. "Maybe someone is taking new positions without waiting for a correction."
The market ignored news about planned sales of government stakes in utility UES EESR.RTS and oil company LUKoil and the postponement of sales in oil company ONAKO until 1998, traders said.
ONAKO's main operating company is Orenburgneft UES rose to $0.1700 from $0.1625 at Wednesday's close, LUKoil was $14.955 after $14.50. Orenburgneft rose to $4.090 from $3.750.

Trinfiko's head of trading Ilya Galtsov forecast domestic buying on hopes that the International Monetary Fund would approve disbursement of overdue tranches of its $10 billion loan to Russia would lead to more gains on Friday.
The IMF board meets on Friday.
